title: Yara and the Vow
premise: August Reyes, a marine biologist who fled to a coastal town after a devastating betrayal, has spent three years treating his heart like a specimen: observed, contained, never at risk. When he inherits half of an orchard deed co-signed by Yara Solano—the estranged childhood friend whose family once owned the land and who vanished after a vow they made as teenagers—he is forced into shared stewardship with the one person who knew him before he learned to hide. As they restore the dying orchard together, August's careful walls crumble, but Yara carries a secret about why she left that could shatter their fragile trust. In the end, August must choose between the containable life he built and the whole-hearted risk of staying, signing the deed—and himself—over to love just before the orchard's last chance at blooming.
about_author: Odile Kavanagh is the pen name of a former orchard keeper's daughter who spent a decade cataloguing sea turtles before turning to fiction. She writes romances about stubborn hearts and stubborn land from a cottage she shares with too many citrus trees.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: August's POV. Three years after a betrayal ended his engagement, August lives by routine: turtle surveys, tide charts, no attachments. A lawyer's letter arrives naming him heir to half an orchard deed—co-signed by Yara Solano, the girl who vanished at seventeen. The beat: dread disguised as irritation; his contained life cracking open.

chapters.title: The Deed That Won't Divide
chapters.summary: August visits the county office hoping to sell his half outright, but the deed contains an old covenant: neither party can transfer without the other's consent. He drives to the orchard intending confrontation and instead finds Yara living in the crumbling farmhouse, equally stunned and equally trapped. The beat: reluctant recognition, old wounds surfacing.

chapters.title: What We Swore Under the Fig Tree
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Flashbacks braid with present-day negotiations: at fifteen, she and August vowed to save her family's failing orchard together, before her father's debts and a family secret drove them apart. She agrees to one season of co-stewardship—nothing more. The beat: guarded hope tangled with guilt over what she never told him.

chapters.title: Grafting Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They begin restoring neglected trees, their hands remembering old rhythms. Small intimacies accumulate—shared thermoses, arguments about pruning, laughter that surprises them both. August's turtle research bleeds into orchard metaphors; Yara notices him noticing her. The beat: warmth rekindling against both their intentions.

chapters.title: The Town That Remembers
chapters.summary: August's POV. Neighbors welcome Yara back but treat August like a ghost returning wrong. At a harvest festival, an old friend of Yara's father lets slip that the Solanos left 'because of what happened to the boy.' August realizes Yara's departure was entangled with his own family. The beat: suspicion taking root where trust was growing.

chapters.title: Rootstock
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Pressed by a storm-damaged grove and August's cold questions, Yara nearly confesses: her father's bankruptcy was caused by August's uncle, who bought the Solano debt and seized the land—a truth that made her feel complicit in stealing August's inheritance of friendship. She retreats instead. The beat: loyalty to family memory versus longing for truth.

chapters.title: Cold Snap
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. An unexpected frost threatens the recovering blossoms; they work through the night saving the trees, but the intimacy breaks when August demands the truth about why she left. Yara deflects; August accuses her of repeating her old vanishing act. She signs papers to release her half of the deed. The beat: heartbreak as self-protection, both retreating behind walls.

chapters.title: The Muscle Remembers
chapters.summary: August's POV. With the sale pending, August returns to his turtles and finds the containment strategy hollow: the heart, he admits, was never containable. His mentor's old letters reveal his uncle's deathbed remorse—and a document proving the uncle tried to return the Solano land years ago. The beat: grief transmuting into resolve; choosing risk over safety.

chapters.title: The Vow, Reclaimed
chapters.summary: Climax. On the day the deed transfers, August stops the sale and stands before the town in the orchard, telling the whole truth—his uncle's theft, Yara's silence born of shame, his own years of hiding. He asks not for forgiveness but to finish the vow they made under the fig tree. Yara, moved, reveals she never signed the release. The beat: truth offered whole, risking everything.

chapters.title: First Bloom
chapters.summary: Resolution. Spring: the orchard blooms for the first time in a decade. August and Yara re-sign the deed as partners—in land and in life—surrounded by the found family of neighbors who stayed to help. August counts turtles still, but now he counts blossoms too, and lets himself be counted. The beat: wholeness; love as stewardship, not possession.
